newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP steel workers to strike 24 hours.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP steel workers to strike 24 hours.

text.p: Steel workers employed by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd voted on Tuesday to strike for 24 hours over wages from Friday, the Australian Workers Union said.
"There was a unanimous endorsement to take industrial action as necessary," AWU state secretary Bob Smith said of the vote taken by steel workers at meeting held earlier.
Smith said if no agreement was reached with BHP, the strikes would continue next year. But Friday's action would be the only stoppage for the remainder of 1996, he added.
BHP's 20,000 unionised steel workers are agitating for pay rises above the 8.5 percent over two years offered by the company.
"That's deemed to be inadequate. We're looking community pay rises (and) we're not seeing anything less than 10 percent," Smith said.
He said the unions' demands were fair given BHP's strong profitability.
A BHP Steel spokesman said the company would not comment on the matter until later in the day.
BHP's 1995/96 net profit was A$1.05 billion, down from A$1.22 billion a year earlier. Its first quarter profits fell 22.8 percent to A$287 million.
But BHP Steel earnings were expected to rise in fiscal 1996/97, the division's chief executive Ron McNeilly told Reuters in an interview in October.
